slides.title: Spoken Tutorial on APIs
slides.narration: Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on **APIs**.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn to,
• Define what an **API** is.
• Explain the role of an **API Key**.
• Identify components of an **API request**.

slides.title: System Requirements
slides.narration: Here I am using a browser on a computer or mobile.

slides.title: Pre-requisites
slides.narration: To follow this tutorial, you should have completed Module 2: Art of the Prompt.

slides.title: What is an API? The Restaurant Waiter
slides.narration:
What is an **API**?
**API** stands for Application Programming Interface.
Think of an **API** like a restaurant waiter.
You give your order, or request, to the waiter.
The waiter takes it to the kitchen, which is like the **AI** model.
Then, the waiter brings back your dish, which is the **AI** response.
So, an **API** acts as a messenger between applications.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a restaurant waiter taking an order from a customer (application) and delivering it to the kitchen (AI model), then bringing back the food (response).

slides.title: What is an API Key? Your Restaurant ID Card
slides.narration:
Now, how does the restaurant know you are a valid customer?
You might show an ID card.
An **API key** is just like your restaurant ID card.
It is a unique identifier, a secret password.
This key authenticates your application.
It proves you are authorized to make requests.
Always keep your **API key** private and secure.
slides.image_prompt: Close-up of a hand holding an ID card labeled 'API Key' next to a restaurant menu, emphasizing authentication.

slides.title: What is an API Request? Placing Your Order
slides.narration:
You place your order with the waiter.
This action is similar to an **API request**.
An **API request** is sending information to an **API**.
You send it to get a specific service.
Your **API key** is usually included for authentication.
It is like placing your order to the waiter.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a customer placing an order with a waiter, with thought bubbles showing 'API Request' and 'API Key'.

slides.title: API Request in Action: A Real-Life Demo
slides.narration:
Let us see an **API request** in action.
Open any food delivery app on your phone.
Tap the search bar and type 'pizza'.
The app sends an **API request** to the server.
This request includes your search query and location.
The server's **API** processes this request.
It finds relevant pizza places.
The **API** sends these results back to your app.
Your app displays them on your screen.
slides.image_prompt: Screen close-up: a smartphone displaying a food delivery app with 'pizza' typed in the search bar, and search results appearing.

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
Let us summarize what we learned.
We defined **APIs** as messengers between applications.
**API keys** are for authenticating your requests.
**API requests** are how you ask for **AI** services.
It is all like ordering food at a restaurant.

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
Now as an assignment,
Observe an everyday app you use.
Can you identify where an **API request** might be happening?
Think about what information is sent and received.
Compare the results.
